subject: Performance calibration + temporary headcount bridging plan
content:
From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rebecca Ortiz <rebecca@talentops.co>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 16:12:00 +0000
Subject: Performance calibration + temporary headcount bridging plan

Hi all,

Brief context: as you know, Olivia (Sr. ML Eng, ML Serving) accepted an internal promotion effective Oct 30th. That leaves a senior IC role on the serving team that is mission-critical for our Q4 rollout (low-latency inference improvements and two customer migrations). The timing overlaps with performance calibration next week and the hiring freeze that the business instituted last quarter.

Ask: I’m requesting an exception for a short-term bridging plan (90 days) to either: 1) hire a contractor through our preferred vendor for up to $45k total, or 2) rotate an internal IC to cover the most urgent milestones while we complete the scoped hire. I prefer option 2 if a fully-available, qualified internal candidate exists, but we need a contingency in case that causes delivery risk.

Why now:
- Delivery risk: two migrations scheduled Nov-Dec that require senior-level troubleshooting and perf tuning.
- Calibration impact: Olivia’s promotion and mid-cycle changes mean we have to avoid overloading remaining seniors during calibration week.
- Cost discipline: proposing a capped contractor spend and a hard end-date (90 days).

Attachments: hc-waiver-form.pdf (blank waiver), org-chart_v3.png (serving team), candidate_briefing.docx (template for contractor brief).

Requested decisions and timeline:
- Decision on contractor vs rotation by Fri Oct 15 (EOD).
- If contractor approved: procurement list + vendor sourcing approved by Finance before offer.
- If rotation chosen: name of interim and re-assignment plan by Mon Oct 18.

Next steps I will take: prepare a short candidate brief and a prioritized handoff checklist. Want to loop in Finance and People Ops for approvals; copying Rebecca for TalentOps awareness.

Thanks,
Michael
Michael Grant
Director, Serving Platform
Redwood Inference

---
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Rebecca Ortiz <rebecca@talentops.co>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 18:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Performance calibration + temporary headcount bridging plan

Thanks Michael — quick clarifying Qs:
1) Which cost center would this contractor be charged to? (serving-platform vs infra)
2) If we consider internal rotation, who would you propose as interim? (we have limited bench capacity)
3) Do we expect this role to be re-opened after 90 days?

My initial thought: try rotation first (lower cost, preserves headcount). Ethan Park has some bandwidth and the ramp would be ~2 weeks. If Ethan isn’t feasible, I’m OK with a contractor but would prefer the cap be closer to $30–35k.

Laura
VP, Product

---
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 09:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Performance calibration + temporary headcount bridging plan

Michael — thanks for the clear write-up. I approve an exception in principle for a 90-day contractor or internal rotation with conditions:
- Spend cap: $35k unless a written waiver is approved by Finance.
- Primary preference: internal rotation (bench > contractor). Please put forward the name(s) and a brief coverage plan.
- No permanent backfill without full HC approval post-review cycle.

Condition: Finance sign-off required before any offer is finalized. Tessa — can People Ops start the waiver workflow and flag any compensation/process implications for performance calibration?

Markus Klein
VP, Engineering

---
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rebecca Ortiz <rebecca@talentops.co>
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 11:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Performance calibration + temporary headcount bridging plan

Thanks — I have started the waiver workflow. Checklist for the team to move this forward:
- Michael: Complete hc-waiver-form.pdf (fields: rationale, duration, spend cap, sign-offs).
- Michael/Laura: Confirm preferred option (rotation candidate or contractor) and provide the interim name(s).
- Finance: Need a line item approval for up to $35k (or higher if Markus signs a waiver). Copy to finance-approvals@redwood.ai.
- TalentOps (Rebecca): If contractor, please confirm vendor list and SOW template; if rotation, confirm impact on candidate pipelines and performance calibration notes.
- Ops: Update org-chart_v3.png and provide a short handoff checklist (deliverable list).

Links and forms: https://docs.redwood.com/internal/hc-waiver/2026-q4 (waiver workflow)
I’ll attach a People Ops checklist to the waiver once Michael fills the form.

Tessa Morgan
Sr. Manager, People Ops

Attachment: People Ops checklist (stub)

Thanks everyone — action items I’m taking this morning:
- I’ll complete hc-waiver-form.pdf and upload it to the waiver workflow by EOD today.
- I’ll reach out to Ethan Park to confirm availability for a rotation; if he’s unavailable, I’ll source a short list of contractors and share the candidate_briefing.docx by tomorrow.
- Schedule: aim to have Finance approval by Oct 16 so we can onboard a contractor (if needed) before Nov migrations.
